item.title: Sebi mulls automatic approval for investments, activities by exchanges
item.description: Sebi has proposed an automatic approval route for certain activities and investments by market infrastructure institutions, subject to financial limits and governance safeguards.
item.content:encoded:
Home / Markets / News / Sebi mulls automatic approval for investments, activities by exchanges

Sebi mulls automatic approval for investments, activities by exchanges Sebi has proposed an automatic approval route for certain activities and investments by market infrastructure institutions, subject to financial limits and governance safeguards.

Sebi has proposed allowing stock exchanges and depositories to undertake certain activities and investments without prior regulatory approval, subject to safeguards. (Photo: Reuters)

Press Trust of India 3 min read Last Updated : Oct 23 2026 | 11:45 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Markets regulator Sebi has proposed allowing stock and depositories to deploy funds and undertake activities related to their core functions without its prior approval, a move aimed at reducing regulatory burden and improving ease of doing business.   In its consultation paper, the Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has proposed an automatic approval route for activities related or incidental to the core functions of exchanges and depositories, subject to specified financial limits and governance safeguards.   The proposal covers market infrastructure institutions (MIIs), which currently require prior Sebi approval for activities involving fund deployment or otherwise, except for treasury investments made under a board-approved investment policy.

"The MIIs (excluding the recognized clearing corporations) may engage in activities whether involving deployment of funds or otherwise, without prior approval of Sebi (herein after referred to as the "automatic route"), in the following routes (A&B) and subject to the financial limits ... and the governance conditions," Sebi said.   Under the proposed framework, the automatic Route A would cover activities undertaken pursuant to Sebi directions, certain transfers of shares within an MII group, and deployment of funds by an operating subsidiary exclusively from its own operational earnings. Also Read

Sebi eases call-recording mandate for research analysts dealing with funds

Whistleblower tipoffs on insider trading up sharply as Sebi gets 25 in FY26 premium

Sebi warns investors against fraudulent WhatsApp stock tip groups

The Route B would cover activities similar in function to those carried out by an MII through an entity regulated by another financial sector regulator in India, provided Sebi has previously approved such activity and its nature remains unchanged.

Also, Sebi has proposed capping aggregate fund deployment under the automatic route in a financial year at the lower of 5 per cent of the MII's net worth as of March 31 of the preceding financial year or the regulatory minimum net worth requirement. Further, the MII's net worth after the proposed deployment should not fall below 1.5 times the minimum net worth prescribed by the regulator.   The proposed framework also mandates governance safeguards, including prior approval of each new activity or fund deployment by the MII's governing board, measures to prevent conflicts of interest, and compliance with fit-and-proper criteria by investee companies, their directors and shareholders.

MIIs would also be required to put in place board-approved standard operating procedures and submit half-yearly reports to   Sebi detailing activities undertaken under the automatic route within 30 days of the end of each half-year.   The regulator said the existing framework imposes the same approval requirement on activities irrespective of their size, nature or risk, creating an additional compliance burden even for small investments that directly support market operations.   It also noted that separate approvals could lead to duplication of regulatory scrutiny in cases where activities are already directed by Sebi or involve entities regulated by other financial sector regulators.   The Securities and Exchange Board of India (Sebi) has sought public comments till November 12 on the proposals.

item.title: Infosys Q2 results: Net profit rises 6.2% to ₹7,823 cr, revenue up 10.7%
item.description: Net profit rises 6.2% to ₹7,823 cr, revenue up 10.2% ...
item.dc:creator: Avik Das
item.content:encoded: Information technology services firm Infosys, the country’s second-largest, has reduced its revenue forecast for 2026-27 because growth in its largest market, the United States (US), is expected to weaken and deflationary pressure from artificial intelligence (AI) is anticipated to increase.  On Friday, the company said it expected revenues to grow 1-2 per cent in constant currency, down from the 1.5-3 per cent it expected three months ago. Its net profit for the second quarter rose 6.2 per cent to ₹7,828 crore while revenues were up 10.7 per cent to ₹49,244 crore, helped by its financial-services, and energy and utilities businesses. While net profit missed analyst estimates, revenues exceeded those.  Analysts polled by Bloomberg had expected net profit and revenues to be ₹7,904 crore and ₹49,108 crore, respectively. Dollar revenues were up 1.3 per cent while in constant-currency terms, the increase was 1.5 per cent, which was just more than Wipro’s 0.6 per cent. The Bengaluru-based company grew at its slowest pace in at least six quarters. On top of it, the outlook was clouded by AI deflationary pressure, lower than expected discretionary spending, sector-specific softness, and an ongoing volatile economic environment. These are expected to make the second half tougher than the first. “It was a soft quarter for us. The volumes were softer and in AI we are also seeing compression. We are only taking up contracts that meet our economic guidelines,” Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and Managing Director (MD) Salil Parekh said. With little visibility on large deals, the impact was evident on Infosys’ US-listed shares, which were down almost 6.4 per cent in pre-market trading. The total contract value of large deals won during the three months of the quarter was $5.2 billion, which included one of more than $2 billion. However, the benefits will kick in from April. Such deals are geared towards cost optimisation and vendor-consolidation projects. They take time to materialise. In a subdued demand, large deals would also mean fierce competition among players, leading to margins being eroded. The positive aspect of the results was AI revenues. Infosys also said its AI revenues accounted for 10.5 per cent of its top line, up from the 8.2 per cent in the first quarter and growing 29 per cent sequentially. That market opportunity, which Parekh held up as a $300 billion opportunity, consists of AI strategy and engineering, the data for AI, process AI, agentic legacy modernisation, physical AI and AI trust. “Although the operating margin remained stable at 21 per cent, the weaker growth outlook is likely to remain the key focus for investors. If Infosys continues to rely on acquisitions to support reported growth without a meaningful recovery in its underlying business, the market could begin to assign it a lower valuation multiple,” Manav Medewala of Mirae Asset Sharekhan wrote in a note. Financial services, the main contributor to revenues, were up 2.1 per cent while energy, utilities and resources increased 7.3 per cent. Retail, which still faces headwinds, was down 7.7 per cent and hi-tech dipped 17.3 per cent. North America revenues dropped 1.5 per cent while those of Europe were up 4.6 per cent. The operating margin was nearly flat at 21.1 per cent with positive currency impacts and higher working days more than offset by acquisition-related efforts. “The second half will be impacted from wage hikes and the continued intensity on pricing,” Chief Financial Officer Jayesh Sanghrajka said. The company added 4,480 employees and the headcount was 332,542 at the end of September. Voluntary attrition was 12.7 per cent and it hired 8,000 freshers in the quarter.

item.title: Apple India revenue grows 32% to cross ₹1 trillion mark in FY26: Tofler
item.description: Phone maker Apple's India revenue grew by over 32 per cent to Rs 1,04,607 crore in FY26, according to the document shared by market intelligence firm Tofler. The company recorded revenue of Rs 79,060.
item.content:encoded:
Home / Companies / News / Apple India revenue grows 32% to cross ₹1 trillion mark in FY26: Tofler

Apple India revenue grows 32% to cross ₹1 trillion mark in FY26: Tofler The company's total expenses for the fiscal were reported at Rs 96,224 crore, Tofler said

(Photo: Reuters)

Press Trust of India New Delhi 1 min read Last Updated : Oct 23 2026 | 11:17 PM IST

Listen to This Article

iPhone maker Apple's India revenue grew by over 32 per cent to Rs 1,04,607 crore in FY26, according to the document shared by market intelligence firm Tofler. The company recorded revenue of Rs 79,060.5 crore in FY25. "Apple India Private Limited provides and markets Apple brand products and software, and reported its revenues for the financial year 2025-26 at Rs 1,04,607 crore, a 32 per cent jump since the last financial year," Tofler said. Apple India net profit grew by 66 per cent to Rs 5,311 crore in the same fiscal. The company's total expenses for the fiscal were reported at Rs 96,224 crore, Tofler said.

(Only the headline and picture of this report may have been reworked by the Business Standard staff; the rest of the content is auto-generated from a syndicated feed.)

item.title: AI-discovered software bugs may trigger more outages, warn cyber experts
item.description: Cybersecurity experts say AI is accelerating the discovery and exploitation of software flaws, raising the risk of further disruptions even as its impact on successful hacks remains uncertain ...
item.content:encoded:
Home / World News / AI-discovered software bugs may trigger more outages, warn cyber experts

AI-discovered software bugs may trigger more outages, warn cyber experts Cybersecurity experts say AI is accelerating the discovery and exploitation of software flaws, raising the risk of further disruptions even as its impact on successful hacks remains uncertain

(Photo: Reuetrs)

Reuters 5 min read Last Updated : Oct 23 2026 | 10:37 PM IST

Listen to This Article

Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) have uncovered a stream of new software vulnerabilities that are almost certain to trigger more disruptions along the lines of the outages that spread across government websites globally this week, according to seven cybersecurity professionals who spoke to Reuters.   AI helped drive a doubling of the number of digital flaws discovered year-on-year, according to research due to be published in the coming days by VulnCheck, a Massachusetts-based threat intelligence firm.   Matthew Prince, the chief executive of digital infrastructure firm Cloudflare, told Reuters he was aware of “a bunch of additional severe vulnerabilities that are present in other pieces of critical software” and predicted busy months ahead as AI surfaced long-hidden weaknesses in the fabric of the internet.

“I think we’re going to have a couple years where every single week it’s going to feel like the sky is falling,” Prince said in an interview on Thursday.   The outages that spread across government sites in Europe and elsewhere beginning on Wednesday happened after the discovery of weaknesses in PHP, a long-established programming language that powers a huge swathe of the internet. Operators have been rushing to fix their software in anticipation of mass exploitation and, because some felt they could not patch the vulnerabilities before hackers exploited them, some simply took their sites offline until they could make them safe.

Also Read

The coming global wealth destruction premium

Microsoft develops AI tool that can diagnose 'sequentially' like doctor

OpenAI shifts valuation to $1.25 trillion as funding talks near final stage

Only 1% of engineers work in FDE roles despite rising AI demand: Report

AI data centre backlash threatens Australia's $70 billion investment boom

VulnCheck researcher Patrick Garrity said the scramble to fix PHP came during an already busy week in cybersecurity. The week also brought disclosures of vulnerabilities in PHP alternative Node.js and streaming programme Plex, breaches tied to AI gateway LiteLLM and development platform Railway, and the revelation that Indian certificate authority eMudhra had used an extraordinarily weak cryptographic key that potentially put users across the internet at risk.   “If we just saw four or five things like this, this week, I would expect we’re going to see a lot more,” Garrity said. “I think there’s going to be a lot more fire drills for anything that’s internet exposed.”

Timelines Shortening   The codebases that run modern programs are sprawling, and mistakes, or “bugs”, that open up potential avenues for exploitation often crop up in unexpected places.   Previously, finding bugs required a baseline level of skill, and taking advantage of those bugs to build digital lockpicks — called “exploits” — could be expected to take weeks or months of work by an experienced professional.   That would, in the past, have provided defenders a little breathing room to fix bugs and gradually roll out software updates.   AI has effectively thrown those assumptions out of the window.   Models can find one bug after another by subjecting codebases to round-the-clock scrutiny and can produce exploits in hours.

Shane Fry, the chief technology officer of Virginia-based RunSafe Security, said the demonstrated performance of AI models over the past few months had effectively laid to rest any doubts over whether they would change the industry.   “What's fundamentally, and unquestionably, changing is the timescale for not only finding vulnerabilities, but how quickly adversaries can weaponize them,” Fry said.   Scary monsters   While all the experts Reuters spoke to agreed that defenders’ timelines were getting shorter, they were split on whether AI would lead to a hacker free-for-all.   Daniel Stenberg, the lead developer of the file transfer tool curl, argued that the vulnerabilities found by AI models tended to be exotic bugs that were difficult for rogue actors to take advantage of. Ramy Rahman, a senior principal solutions engineer at cybersecurity company ArmorCode, said “more disclosed vulnerabilities do not automatically mean more successful attacks."

There was tentative evidence of that around the PHP vulnerability that drew worldwide concern this week. Threat intelligence firm Hunt.io said that — like Amazon and Cloudflare — it had seen aggressive attempts to take advantage of the bug. But the firm’s head of research, Esteban Borges, said that, as of 2 p.m. Eastern Time on Thursday (1800 GMT), the cybercriminals he tracked appeared to have failed to cobble together a working tool to take advantage of it.   Prince, of Cloudflare, told Reuters he had seen anecdotal evidence of compromises linked to the PHP vulnerability.   The deluge of AI-driven discoveries might rattle the industry but would be a net positive in the end, he said, comparing it to slaying the monsters in a haunted house.

The confrontation might be scary, he said, but leaving the monsters to lurk quietly behind closed doors was far worse.   “The reality is, we’re going to get a lot of this stuff cleaned up,” he said.   Japan to simulate cyberattacks    Japan said on Friday it will set up a team to simulate  cyberattacks using artificial intelligence (AI) to identify weaknesses in technology systems as organisations scramble to curtail risks from flaws in the PHP programming language that underpins much of the internet. Highlighting the extent of the disruption, Japan’s third-largest mobile carrier, SoftBank, said on Friday it was suspending its emergency alert system for mobile users.That means customers will not receive early warnings for earthquakes, tsunami alerts or disaster and evacuation information.
